summary: Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist who earned his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson among others. He was attested as a professor at Kyoto University in 2019.

Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975) and worked at the Museum of history of religion (~1975–1988).

Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig. He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv, where he became full professor and department head in 1917.

András Róna-Tas is a linguist, Tibetologist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. He was a professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002) and president of IATS (~1979–1989).

André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, and EPHE, supervised by Jean Filliozat. He served as Directeur d'Études at the EPHE (1956–1973) and Directeur at the Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the EPHE. His academic posts included the University of Strasbourg (1957–1960), the EPHE (~1957–1972), and the Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Laval University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris-Sorbonne University, and held a post at Laval University around 1980.

André Godard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1903–1910) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1953).

André Leroi-Gourhan was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at the University of Paris (~1928–1944) under Marcel Mauss. He held positions at Musée Guimet (1940–1943), the University of Paris (~1956–1969), and the Collège de France (1969–1982).

André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and Humboldt University of Berlin under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the EPHE (~1938–1946), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1970).
André Mazon was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1904) and Charles University (~1904–1905). He served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the Collège de France and completed doctoral work under Olivier Lacombe and Louis Renou. He served as director of IFHA (~1959–1964) and Directeur de Recherche at CNRS (~1964–1985).
André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady at the University of Leipzig (~1904–1908), where he also held an academic post.

André-Georges Haudricourt was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Institut national agronomique, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at CNRS (~1940–1979), EFEO (~1947–1949), and Paris Descartes University (~1970–1979).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and archaeology. She earned her doctorate at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She was attested as a professor at Rutgers University in 2005.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology. She held positions at Freie Universität Berlin and was attested as a researcher at the University of Oulu in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, having studied under Nalini Devdas, and was attested as an assistant professor at Carleton University in 2008.

Angela Zito is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1980–1989) and became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University around 1996.

Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She was an assistant professor at Frankfurt (1993–2001) and took a practical philosophy chair at the University of Basel in 2001.

Angelika Malinar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her PhD (1991) and Habilitation (1998) at the University of Tübingen. She taught at SOAS (~2000–2007) and became an extraordinary professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.
